news.title: Oil Prices Caught Between a Looming Glut and Middle East Turmoil
news.summary: Oil prices have traded in a narrow range over the past few sessions as forecasts of a coming surplus collide with continued attacks and stalled diplomacy in the Middle East. A run of agency reports this month has pushed expectations toward oversupply and weighed on crude. Brent crude was up 0.22% at $92.18 per barrel in early trade on Friday, well below its October levels above $110 but little changed from the start of the week, while WTI crude had gained 0.35% to $82.73 per barrel. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its November Oil…

analysis.summary: Crude prices are range-bound as agency forecasts of an upcoming supply glut offset ongoing Middle East attacks and stalled diplomacy.
analysis.rationale: The text explicitly cites opposing price drivers: oversupply expectations from recent agency reports exerting downward pressure and persistent Middle East conflict supporting prices.

news.title: Argentine Energy Firms Rush to Sell Bonds Before the 2027 Election
news.summary: Argentina’s energy sector is having a banner year. The first half of 2026 saw the South American nation’s best energy trade balance in half a decade as exports boomed thanks to a drop in exports out of the Middle East and strong production numbers out of the Vaca Muerta shale play. And Argentina’s energy export boom isn’t over. This week, major underwriter Banco Santander announced that a wave of dollar bond sales out of Argentina is projected to extend into the first half of 2027 as the nation’s energy sector continues…

analysis.summary: Argentine energy firms are accelerating dollar bond sales ahead of the 2027 election amid strong Vaca Muerta output and export growth.
analysis.rationale: While rising Argentine production and exports represent incremental supply, the article focuses on corporate debt issuance and notes exports rose partly due to lower Middle East shipments, leaving no clear net directional signal for global crude.

news.title: Norway’s Gas Sales Surge Nearly 20% as Europe Braces for Winter
news.summary: Norway’s daily gas sales jumped nearly 20% in October and were 5.6% above year-earlier levels. The rebound comes as the EU heads into winter with its gas storage facilities less than 70% full. Norway sold 11 billion cubic meters of natural gas in October, up 2.1 billion cubic meters from September, according to preliminary figures from the Norwegian Offshore Directorate. Daily sales averaged 355.6 million cubic meters, up from a revised 296.8 million in September and 2.2% above the regulator’s forecast. EU gas storage was 69.8% full…

analysis.summary: Norway's October natural gas sales jumped nearly 20% month-on-month and beat forecasts as EU gas storage sits below 70% entering winter.
analysis.rationale: The report covers European natural gas supply and storage without mentioning crude oil, providing insufficient textual evidence for a direct crude price impact.

news.title: China’s Oil Imports from Persian Gulf Jump to Wartime High
news.summary: China’s crude oil imports from the Persian Gulf surged by 42.4% in October from September, to the highest level since the Iran war began, as supply via the Strait of Hormuz rebounded and Gulf producers slashed prices for their crude to attract buyers amid record-high freight rates. China imported 19.7 million tons of crude oil from the Persian Gulf producers, excluding Iran, in October, a 42.4% jump from the previous month, per calculations by the South China Morning Post based on Chinese customs data released on Friday. analysis.summary: China's October crude imports from the Persian Gulf jumped 42.4% as Strait of Hormuz flows rebounded and Gulf producers cut prices.
analysis.rationale: Rebounding Strait of Hormuz supply and producer price discounts indicate bearish supply easing, while the sharp jump in Chinese import volume points to resilient buying demand.
